chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from his father, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام handed me seven hundred dīnārs and said: “O ʿUdhāfir, spend it in some enterprise.” And he said: “I do not do this out of greed on my part, but I wanted Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to see me exposing myself to His benefits.”

ʿUdhāfir said: So I made a profit of one hundred dīnārs in it. Then I said to him during the ṭawāf, “May I be your ransom, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has provided one hundred dīnārs in profit through it.” He said: “Record it in my capital.”

key_terms.اصْرِفْهَا: Put it to use in a transaction or enterprise
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: A gold coin used here as trade capital
key_terms.مُتَعَرِّضًا لِفَوَائِدِهِ: Actively seeking and placing oneself in the way of Allah’s benefits and gains

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about trade, profit, and seeking Allah’s bounty?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام entrusted capital for trade and clarified that doing so was not from greed, but from seeking the bounty of Allah. It shows the permissibility and dignity of lawful earning and frames commercial activity as a means of engaging with divine provision.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3581 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdullah (as), handed me seven hundred dinars and said:
"O 'Udhafir, invest it in something."
Imam (as) then added: "I am not doing this out of greed, but I wish for Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, to see me seeking His bounties."

Udhafir said: I earned a profit of one hundred dinars from it. So, while performing Tawaf, I said to him: "May I be your ransom! Allah (swt), the Exalted, has grant a profit of one hundred dinars in it."
Imam (as) replied: "Add it to my capital."
